stops.name: Medina, retirement and remorse
stops.campa: Back within her own chamber, Aishah withdraws from all further politics for the rest of her life, and is heard afterward to weep at the mention of the Camel, wishing aloud that she had died twenty years before that day rather than ridden out of Mecca on it. She gives away in charity what income comes to her until, it is said, she keeps nothing back for herself even at her own table, as though the giving were a penance the years of teaching alone could not complete.

stops.name: Medina, teaching to the end, the vast legacy of hadith
stops.campa: Into old age the curtain of her room still opens to questioners: jurists, governors' wives, her own great-nephews, come to hear what only she remembers. By the time she dies more than two thousand sayings and reports of the Messenger will be traced back to her alone, more than from any other of his wives and among the very most of any Companion living or dead — on prayer, fasting, marriage, medicine, grief, and the small kindnesses of an ordinary house that no one else had thought worth setting down.

stops.name: Medina, her death on the seventeenth of Ramadan
stops.campa: In the sixty-sixth or sixty-seventh year of her life, in the same small rooms she has kept since her wedding, Aishah dies during the caliphate of Mu'awiya, having outlived the husband she married as a child by nearly half a century and having become, in the space of that half-century, the single richest channel through which his words reached every generation after him. She leaves instructions that she be buried not beside him in the crowded chamber but out among her sister-wives, saying she has done a thing since his death that she cannot let a grave beside him seem to absolve.
stops.quote: I did something major after the Messenger of Allah. Do not bury me with them; bury me with my companions in al-Baqi', so that I not be praised thereby.
stops.quote_source: Her deathbed will, cited in Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat al-Kubra (Kitab al-Nisa, vol. 8); the burial instruction also in Sahih al-Bukhari 1391

stops.name: Jannat al-Baqi, buried by torchlight among the Prophet's wives
stops.campa: As she wished, she is carried after the night prayer to al-Baqi, the open burial ground of Medina, not into the crowded chamber where the Messenger, her father, and Umar lie together. Abu Hurayrah, last of the great narrators of her own generation, leads the funeral prayer over her by the light of cloths soaked in oil and set burning, for the night is dark and the mourners many. She is laid among the other Mothers of the Believers, closing, in that plain grave under torchlight, the road that began in a besieged house in Mecca.
